Partially signed transaction

A partially signed transaction is a data structure that lets several parties build and sign a transaction together.[1] The format was proposed in 2017 and adopted by most wallets within a few years.[2]

History

Before the format existed, each wallet used its own way to pass unsigned transactions around.[3] Hardware wallets in particular needed the previous outputs to show the fee.

Format

The structure is a set of key-value maps, one for the transaction, one per input and one per output. Unknown keys are kept, so newer fields survive older software.
